The array already has 4 slots — the leading comma makes slot 0 empty (the kick step), and the three `fs3(…)` fill slots 1–3. Where the trailing comma genuinely matters is when an array **ends on a rest** — e.g. `[ c3, , , ]` is only 3 slots because JS throws the final separating comma away, so you'd write `[ c3, , , , ]` (or `[c3, , , null]`) to get 4. Same principle, it just isn't triggered here since your last slot is a note.
